Markus — forwarding my notes after a quick review of the attached OrderForm-v3_redline.pdf. High-level guidance below and a suggested conservative approach so ops can proceed without waiting on a full MSA amendment.

-----Begin Legal Notes-----
1) Signer authorization: we accept subsidiary delegated signing for order values <= $250k provided the Order Form explicitly references Section 7.3 of the MSA (signatory authority) and the purchaser provides a Board or CFO delegation certificate. For > $250k, we need an explicit corporate resolution or signatory certificate and a one-off exception approval from Legal Ops.

2) Liability/Indemnity redlines: the customer's redline to Sections 4 and 9 remove some of Redwood's limitation of liability language. We should push back on any carveouts that expand customer indemnities to third-party data processors. Recommend tracking these as MSA-level issues and not accepting them on the Order Form.

3) PO Ack SLA and EDI: we can operationally support 24h ack but it requires a dedicated priority lane and SFTP/EDIFACT configuration. If Hearthline can accept 48–72h for standard onboarding, we will avoid the additional integration work. Ops should surface the delta and pricing impact if Hearthline wants 24h acks.

4) Suggested operational path: accept the Order Form redline with two edits — (a) reference MSA Section 7.3 for delegated signers and (b) include an explicit PO Ack SLA of 48h in the order. All MSA redlines to liability/indemnity remain open and are not folded into acceptance. That lets procurement sign and we complete an MSA amendment separately if required.

Attachments: legal-orderform-checklist.pdf (stub)
-----End Legal Notes-----

Mateo — can you take the Ariba field mapping and produce a definitive field-to-field crosswalk (Ariba field name -> Redwood vendor attribute) and call out where normalization or parsing is required (tax jurisdiction, remit-to country code, multi-ship to)? I started a checklist and put it in the shared Drive link.
